264	
265	// gitEmptyConfigPath returns the path to a config file suitable for use as
266	// GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL/GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM. We use a real file instead of
267	// os.DevNull because git on Windows cannot open NUL as a config file.
268	//
269	// The file is not strictly empty: it pins background maintenance off so that
270	// no detached `git gc`/`git maintenance` process lingers after a test holding
271	// an open handle on the temp repo's .git/objects. Such a lingering process
272	// races t.TempDir()'s deferred RemoveAll and fails the test with
273	// "directory not empty" (see COR-394). Suppressing it centrally keeps every
274	// git-shelling test that uses GitIsolatedEnv/IsolateGitConfigEnv safe.
275	var gitEmptyConfig string
276	var gitEmptyConfigOnce sync.Once
277	
278	// EnvGitHermetic, when set to a non-empty value, makes gitEmptyConfigPath append
279	// per-host HTTP proxy config that routes git HTTPS transport to real external
280	// hosts (github.com, gitlab.com) through an unroutable loopback proxy. Any test
281	// whose git commands accidentally dial those hosts then fails fast (connection
282	// refused at 127.0.0.1:1) instead of reaching the network or prompting for
283	// credentials. It is opt-in per test process — the integration TestMain sets it
284	// — so unit test packages that don't set it are unaffected. Because
285	// GitIsolatedEnv strips all inherited GIT_CONFIG_* env, this config must live in
286	// the file GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL points at (this one), not in GIT_CONFIG_* env
287	// entries.
288	//
289	// A dead proxy (not url.insteadOf) is used deliberately: insteadOf rewrites the
290	// effective URL that git reports on read, which breaks production code that
291	// resolves the origin URL to detect the forge (e.g. `entire trail`). The proxy
292	// blocks transport only, leaving the configured URL string intact, and is scoped
293	// per host so loopback (127.0.0.1) test servers are never proxied.
294	//
295	// Regression class: tests accidentally hitting live github.com / the macOS
296	// keychain (#1463, 53bc37a88).
297	const EnvGitHermetic = "ENTIRE_TEST_GIT_HERMETIC"
298	
299	// hermeticGitConfig routes HTTPS transport to real external hosts through a dead
300	// loopback proxy. Loopback test servers (127.0.0.1) and file:// / bare-path
301	// remotes are not proxied, so the in-process HTTPS git server still works. Only
302	// HTTPS is covered — the accidental-dial regression class is HTTPS fetches; SSH
303	// (git@…) to a real host fails on its own without credentials.
304	const hermeticGitConfig = "[http \"https://github.com/\"]\n" +
305		"\tproxy = http://127.0.0.1:1\n" +
306		"[http \"https://gitlab.com/\"]\n" +
307		"\tproxy = http://127.0.0.1:1\n"
308	
309	func gitEmptyConfigPath() string {
310		gitEmptyConfigOnce.Do(func() {
311			f, err := os.CreateTemp("", "git-isolation-config-*")
312			if err != nil {
313				panic("create git isolation config: " + err.Error())
314			}
315			content := "[gc]\n\tauto = 0\n\tautoDetach = false\n[maintenance]\n\tauto = false\n[fetch]\n\twriteCommitGraph = false\n"
316			if os.Getenv(EnvGitHermetic) != "" {
317				content += hermeticGitConfig
318			}
319			_, err = f.WriteString(content)
320			if err != nil {
321				panic("write git isolation config: " + err.Error())
322			}
323			if err := f.Close(); err != nil {
324				panic("close git isolation config: " + err.Error())
325			}
326			gitEmptyConfig = f.Name()
327		})
328		return gitEmptyConfig
329	}
330	
331	// GitIsolatedEnv returns os.Environ() with git isolation variables set.
332	// This prevents user/system git config (global gitignore, aliases, etc.) from
333	// affecting test behavior. Use this for any exec.Command that runs git or the
334	// CLI binary in integration tests.
335	//
336	// See https://git-scm.com/docs/git#Documentation/git.txt-GITCONFIGGLOBAL
337	//
338	// Every inherited GIT_CONFIG_* entry is filtered out — including
339	// GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS and the indexed KEY_/VALUE_ pairs that can inject
340	// `git -c` overrides — so our explicit isolation overrides take effect
341	// regardless of parent env.
342	func GitIsolatedEnv() []string {
343		env := os.Environ()
344		filtered := make([]string, 0, len(env)+2)
345		for _, e := range env {
346			if isGitConfigEnv(e) {
347				continue
348			}
349			filtered = append(filtered, e)
350		}
351		return append(filtered,
352			"GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL="+gitEmptyConfigPath(), // Isolate from user's global git config (e.g. global gitignore)
353			"GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM="+gitEmptyConfigPath(), // Isolate from system git config
354		)
355	}
356	
357	// IsolateGitConfigEnv applies the same git config isolation to the current
358	// process. Use this in tests that exercise production code paths which invoke
359	// git with os.Environ(). All inherited GIT_CONFIG_* variables are cleared
360	// before the isolation overrides are set, so values such as
361	// GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS or indexed KEY_/VALUE_ overrides cannot leak into
362	// child git invocations.
363	func IsolateGitConfigEnv(t *testing.T) {
364		t.Helper()
365	
366		for _, e := range os.Environ() {
367			key, _, ok := strings.Cut(e, "=")
368			if !ok {
369				continue
370			}
371			if strings.HasPrefix(key, "GIT_CONFIG_") {
372				t.Setenv(key, "")
373			}
374		}
375	
376		t.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL", gitEmptyConfigPath())
377		t.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM", gitEmptyConfigPath())
378		t.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM", "1")
379		t.Setenv("GIT_CONFIG_COUNT", "0")
380	}
381	
382	func isGitConfigEnv(e string) bool {
383		return strings.HasPrefix(e, "GIT_CONFIG_")
384	}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Rewrite bare exec git blocks in strategy/hooks_test.go to testutil.RunGit."""
import re
import sys

path = sys.argv[1]
src = open(path, encoding="utf-8").read()

# Pattern A: run-and-fatal block.
#   <indent>cmd :=|= exec.CommandContext(ctx, "git", <args>)
#   <indent>cmd.Dir = <dir>
#   <indent>if err := cmd.Run(); err != nil {
#   <indent>\tt.Fatalf(...)
#   <indent>}
block_a = re.compile(
    r'(?P<i>[\t]+)cmd (?::=|=) exec\.CommandContext\(ctx, "git"(?P<args>(?:, "[^"]*")*)\)\n'
    r'(?P=i)cmd\.Dir = (?P<dir>[\w.]+)\n'
    r'(?P=i)if err := cmd\.Run\(\); err != nil \{\n'
    r'(?P=i)\tt\.Fatalf\([^\n]*\)\n'
    r'(?P=i)\}\n'
)


def repl_a(m: re.Match) -> str:
    return f'{m.group("i")}testutil.RunGit(t, {m.group("dir")}{m.group("args")})\n'


# Pattern B: output-capture block (rev-parse).
block_b = re.compile(
    r'(?P<i>[\t]+)cmd (?::=|=) exec\.CommandContext\(ctx, "git"(?P<args>(?:, "[^"]*")*)\)\n'
    r'(?P=i)cmd\.Dir = (?P<dir>[\w.]+)\n'
    r'(?P=i)output, err :?= cmd\.Output\(\)\n'
    r'(?P=i)if err != nil \{\n'
    r'(?P=i)\tt\.Fatalf\([^\n]*\)\n'
    r'(?P=i)\}\n'
)


def repl_b(m: re.Match) -> str:
    return f'{m.group("i")}output := testutil.RunGit(t, {m.group("dir")}{m.group("args")})\n'

    print(f"removing {var} at {path}:{line}: {lines[line-1].strip()}")
    del lines[line - 1]
    open(f, "w").writelines(lines)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Migrate testutil git-isolation delegates to gitenv everywhere."""
import os
import re
import sys

ROOT = sys.argv[1]
GITENV_IMPORT = '"github.com/entireio/cli/cmd/entire/cli/testutil/gitenv"'

REPL = [
    ("testutil.GitIsolatedEnv()", "gitenv.Isolated()"),
    ("testutil.IsolateGitConfigEnv(", "gitenv.IsolateProcess("),
    ("testutil.RunGit(", "gitenv.Run("),
    ("testutil.EnvGitHermetic", "gitenv.EnvHermetic"),
]

changed = []
for dirpath, dirs, files in os.walk(ROOT):
    if ".git" in dirs:
        dirs.remove(".git")
    for fn in files:
        if not fn.endswith(".go"):
            continue
        p = os.path.join(dirpath, fn)
        if p.endswith("testutil/gitenv/gitenv.go"):
            continue
        src = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
        orig = src
        for old, new in REPL:
            src = src.replace(old, new)
        if src == orig:
            continue
        if GITENV_IMPORT not in src:
            # insert into the import block
            m = re.search(r"^import \(\n", src, re.M)
            if not m:
                print(f"NO IMPORT BLOCK: {p}")
                continue
            src = src[: m.end()] + "\t" + GITENV_IMPORT + "\n" + src[m.end() :]
        open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(src)
        changed.append(os.path.relpath(p, ROOT))

print(f"{len(changed)} files changed")
for c in changed:
    print(" ", c)

content.text:
Both done — branch `paul/guard-grep-no-color`, unpushed, suite green (86 packages + Vogon canary).

**e2e:** yes. Added `gitenv.IsolateMain()` (os.Setenv-based, since `TestMain` has no `*testing.T`) and e2e's `TestMain` now calls it instead of hand-writing an empty gitconfig. Bonus fix: e2e previously set only `GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL`, so system config and inherited `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS` still leaked — `IsolateMain` covers both. The Vogon canary passed against this, which exercises the real e2e harness.

**Why delegates:** only to avoid touching the 22 caller files in the extraction commit — inertia, not design. You're right there's no reason to keep two spellings, so they're gone: all ~80 callers now call `gitenv.Isolated` / `gitenv.IsolateProcess` / `gitenv.Run` / `gitenv.EnvHermetic` directly, the testutil delegates are deleted, and testutil's own git helpers (`GitAddForce`, `CreateBranch`, `AddRemote`, `GitUpdateRef`, `GitReset`, `GitCheckoutNewBranch`) collapsed to `gitenv.Run` one-liners. `gitenv` is the single implementation everywhere.

One self-inflicted cleanup: my tree-wide goimports pass regrouped imports in 159 files the migration never touched; commit 707d66c52 restores them, so the net diff is only the real change.

Branch now: 7 commits (guard fix → isolation extraction → migration). Squash-merge will read cleanest.

Not hung — it's the Entire pre-push hook, and it's progressing. What's happening:

1. This repo's `origin` is `entire://aws-ap-southeast-2.entire.io/gh/entireio/cli`, so the push runs the full Entire pre-push path.
2. The hook found **16 queued unpushed checkpoint refs** (today's Claude sessions in these worktrees, plus a backlog — the oldest ULID is `01KZQ…`, well before today) and is pushing them to `entire://…/gh/entireio/cli-checkpoints` before your branch ref goes.
3. Each stage does cross-continent round-trips through `git-remote-entire` (I watched a `--filter=blob:none` negotiation fetch spawn and complete between two `ps` samples — so it's advancing, not deadlocked).
4. I made it worse: my first push attempt hit the tool's 2-minute timeout and was killed mid-hook, throwing away that progress; the retry restarted the whole backlog drain.

The `git push` child has been at it ~6 minutes with only ~3s CPU — it's network-bound on the ap-southeast-2 checkpoint sync, not spinning.

Separately: 16 refs taking many minutes looks like a real perf issue in the git-refs checkpoint push path (per-ref negotiation round-trips?) — worth a look once this PR is up, but I'm not chasing it now.

Next: I'll let the background push finish and open the PR when the branch lands. If you'd rather not wait, kill it and run `git push --no-verify` yourself — the refs backend fails soft (checkpoint refs stay queued for the next push; nothing under-redacted ships).

import os
import re

ROOT = sys.argv[1]
V = r"[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9]*"
CTX = r"(?:ctx|context\.Background\(\)|t\.Context\(\))"
HEAD = (
    rf'(?P<i>\t+)(?P<v>{V}) (?::=|=) exec\.Command(?:Context)?\((?:{CTX}, )?"git"'
    rf"(?P<args>.*?)\)(?: //nolint[^\n]*)?\n"
    rf"(?P=i)(?P=v)\.Dir = (?P<dir>[\w.\[\]]+)\n"
    rf"(?P=i)(?P=v)\.Env = testutil\.GitIsolatedEnv\(\)\n"
)

# D: combined output consumed only by require.NoError message
pat_d = re.compile(
    HEAD
    + rf"(?P=i)\w+, err (?::=|=) (?P=v)\.CombinedOutput\(\)\n"
    + rf"(?P=i)require\.NoError\(t, err, [^\n]*\)\n"
)
# E: same, then `return string(out)`
pat_e = re.compile(
    HEAD
    + rf"(?P=i)(?P<o>\w+), err (?::=|=) (?P=v)\.CombinedOutput\(\)\n"
    + rf"(?P=i)require\.NoError\(t, err, [^\n]*\)\n"
    + rf"(?P=i)return string\((?P=o)\)\n"
)
# F: Output, bare require.NoError, return trimmed
pat_f = re.compile(
    HEAD
    + rf"(?P=i)(?P<o>\w+), err (?::=|=) (?P=v)\.Output\(\)\n"
    + rf"(?P=i)require\.NoError\(t, err\)\n"
    + rf"(?P=i)return strings\.TrimSpace\(string\((?P=o)\)\)\n"
)
# G: Run with Fatalf if-block
pat_g = re.compile(
    HEAD
    + rf"(?P=i)if err := (?P=v)\.Run\(\); err != nil \{{\n"
    + rf"(?P=i)\tt\.Fatalf\([^\n]*\)\n"
    + rf"(?P=i)\}}\n"
)


def run(m):
    return f'{m.group("i")}testutil.RunGit(t, {m.group("dir")}{m.group("args")})\n'


def ret(m):
    return f'{m.group("i")}return testutil.RunGit(t, {m.group("dir")}{m.group("args")})\n'


def rett(m):
    return (
        f'{m.group("i")}return strings.TrimSpace('
        f'testutil.RunGit(t, {m.group("dir")}{m.group("args")}))\n'
    )


counts = {}
for dirpath, dirs, files in os.walk(ROOT):
    if ".git" in dirs:
        dirs.remove(".git")
    for fn in files:
        if not fn.endswith(".go"):
            continue
        p = os.path.join(dirpath, fn)
        src = open(p, encoding="utf-8").read()
        orig = src
        for name, pat, sub in [("e", pat_e, ret), ("f", pat_f, rett), ("d", pat_d, run), ("g", pat_g, run)]:
            n = len(pat.findall(src))
            if n:
                counts[name] = counts.get(name, 0) + n
                src = pat.sub(sub, src)
        if src != orig:
            open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(src)
print(counts)
